Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City y,wvy dilqgov.ph DILG OPINION No. 144 s. 2022 November 9, 2022 HON. SOL F. MATUGAS Mayor, Municipality of General Luna Province of Surigao del Norte Dear Mayor Matugas: This has reference to your letter asking for intervention on the implementation of Section 444 (b)(3)(v) of the Local Government Code of 1991 as well as Municipal Ordinance No. 026-22, series of 2022 and Municipal Ordinance No. 006-12-05, series of 2005, the "Revenue Code of the Municipality of General Luna, Province of Surigao del Norte. " The following are the antecedent facts as culled from the documents forwarded to the Central Office: On September 14, 2022, you issued two (2) separate mayor's permits for the conduct of two (2) eventsl pursuant to Section 444 (b) (3)(v) of the Local Govemment Code of 1991, Municipal Ordinance No, 026-22, series of 2022 and Municipal Ordinance No. 006-12-05, series of 2005 or the Revenue Code of the Municipality of General Luna; • On September 19, 2022, you received a letter dated September 16, 2022 from Governor Robert Lyndon S. Barbers of Surigao del Norte informing the former that he will also be holding a ISt Govemor's National Surfing Competition on October 2-7, 2022 at Tuazon Point (a.k.a. Tuazon Point); Since the event of the Provincial Government is in conflict with the events previously issued with mayors permit, you wrote Govemor Barbers through a letter dated September 19, 2022 informing him of the impending conflict; On September 22, 2022, Governor Barbers informed you that the former need not secure a mayor's permit for his ISt Governor's Cup National Surfing Competition which he proposed to be held on October 2-7, 2022 since the Provincial Govemor is authorized under Section 465 of the Local Government Code of 1991 ; On October 4, 2022, you wrote a letter to PCapt Alex A Celiz requesting the 1 ISt Mayor Sol Matugas National Surfing Competition, International Surfing Qualifier to be conducted on September 28 to October 6, 2022 and 26th Siargao International Surfing Cup to be conducted on on October 7-21, 2022. Both event are to be held in Tuazon Point. On the other hand, thelSt Governor's Cup National Surfing Competition is proposed to be held on October 2 to 7, 2022 in the same place, the Tuazon Point. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

latter to implement Memorandum Order No. SFM-036 s 2022 requesting the latter to stop the ISt Governor's Cup activity; • On October 6, 2022, it was reported that the ISt Governors Cup activity was cancelled2. The main issue to be addressed is whether or not the Governor, when holding an activity within a municipality such as the ISt Governor's Cup National Surfing Competition, need to secure mayor's permit from the said municipality? Regardless of the cancellation of the activity, this Department deemed it prudent to provide guidance on the matter. Well-settled in our jurisdiction pursuant to Sections 444 (b)(3)(iv) and 455 (b)(3)(iv) of Republic Act No. 7160 (RA 7160) that only cities and municipalities issue mayors or business permits. Relatively, Section 152 (c) of RA 7160 is instructive as to what activities need the issuance of a mayor's or business permit, to wit: "(c) Barangay Clearance - No city or municipality mav issue any license or permit for any business or activity unless a clearance is first obtained from the Barangay where such business or activity is located or conducted. For such clearance, the Sangguniang Barangay may impose a reasonable fee. The application for clearance shall be acted upon within seven (7) working days from the filing thereof. In the event that the clearance is not issued within the said period, the city or municipality may issue the said license or permit." (Emphasis Supplied) The afore-quoted provision is very clear that the mayor's permit is to be issued to any businesses put up within its jurisdiction and to ANY ACTIVITY conducted therein. The mayor's permit is a regulatory measure exercised by the city/municipality pursuant to the delegated police power given by the Congress to the local government units. In a number of jurisprudence, the Supreme Court comprehensively discussed the nature of mayor's permit. In the case of Roble Arrastre vs. Villaflor, et al.,3 the Supreme Court held: "Section of the Local Government Code of 1991 takes its cue from Section 16 thereof. which is largely an exercise of deleqated police power. We said: https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1676448/s urigao-del-norte-gov-cancels-su ding-tilt-amid-poli tica l- 2 tension. Last accessed on October 24, 2022. 3 G.R. 128509, August 22, 2006.

The qeneral welfare clause is the deleqation in statutory form of the police power of the State to LGUs. Through this. LGUs may prescribe requlations to protect the lives. health, and property of their constituents and maintain peage and order within their respective territorial iurisdictions. Accordingly, we have upheld enactments providing, for instance, the regulation of gambling, the occupation of rig drivers, the installation and operation of pinball machines, the maintenance and operation of cockpits, the exhumation and transfer of corpses from public burial grounds, and the operation of hotels, motels, and lodging houses as valid exercises by local legislatures of the police power under the general welfare clause. Section 444(b)(3)(iv) of the Local Government Code of 1991 , whereby the power of the respondent mayor to issue license and permits is circumscribed, is a manifestation of the delegated police power of a municipal corporation." (Emphasis Supplied) Similarly, in Lacap vs. Sandiganbayan4, viz: "As Section 444(b)(3)(iv) so states, the power of the municipal mayor to issue licenses is pursuant to Section 16 of the Local Government Code of 1991, which declares: SEC. 16. General Welfare. - Every local government unit shall exercise the powers expressly granted, those necessarily implied therefrom, as well as powers necessary, appropriate, or incidental for its efficient and effective governance, and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare. Within their respective territorial jurisdictions, local govemment units shall ensure and support, among other things, the preservation and enrichment of culture, promote health and safety, enhance the right of the people to a balanced ecology, encourage and support the development of appropriate and self-reliant scientific and technological capabilities, improve public morals, enhance economic prosperity and social justice, promote full employment among their residents, maintain peace and order, and preserve the comfort and convenience of their inhabitants. Section 16, known as the general welfare clause, encapsulates the delegated police power to local governments. Local qovernment units exercise police power throuqh their respective Ieqislative bodies. Evidently. the Local Government Code of 1991 is unequivocal that the municipal mayor has the power to issue licenses and permits and suspend or revoke the same for anv violation of the conditions upon which said licenses or permits had been issued. pursuant to law or ordinance. x x x (Emphasis Supplied) 4 G.R. No. 198162, June 21, 2017.

Also, in the case of The City of Bacolod vs. Phuture Visions Co., Inc.5: "xxx while the authority of city mayors to issue or grant licenses and business permits is granted by the Local Government Code (LGC), which also vests local government units with corporate powers, one of which is the power to sue and be sued, this Court has held that the power to issue or qrant licenses and business permits is not an exercise of the government's proprietary function. Instead. it is in an exercise of the police power of the State. erqo a governmental act. This is clearly elucidated by the Court in Acebedo Optical Company, Inc. v. The Honorable Court of Appeals: The Court of Appeals erred in adjudging subject business permit as having been issued by respondent City Mayor in the performance of proprietary functions of Iligan City. As hereinabove elaborated upon, the issuance of business licenses and permits bv a municipality or city is essentiallv requlatorv in nature. The authority. which devolved upon local qovernment units to issue or qrant such licenses or permits. is essentially in the exercise of the police power of the State within the contemplation of the qeneral welfare clause of the Local Government Code. (Emphasis Supplied) Considerably, the mayor's permit is issued as an exercise of delegated police power in relation to the promotion of the general welfare of the people in the LGUs. The Sanggunian of the concemed LGUs pursuant to Section 444 (b)(3)(iv) of RA 7160 may enact an ordinance providing the guidelines/procedure as to the requirement, circumstances, and limitations relative to the issuance of Mayor's permit in accordance with existing relevant national laws and issuances as well as jurisprudence relative thereto. Compliant to the provision of RA 7160, the Municipality of General Luna enacted ordinances pertaining to the issuance of mayors permit relative to the conduct of surfing activities within their jurisdiction, namely: 1) Municipal Ordinance No. 006-12-05, series of 2005 or the Revenue Code of the Municipality of General Luna, Province of Surigao del Norte wherein Section 41.1.01 thereof requires any person who shall conduct, or hold any program, or activity involving the grouping of people within the jurisdiction of this municipality to obtain a Mayor's Permit with corresponding fee; and 2) Municipal Ordinance No. 026-22, series of 2022, which provides that the conduct of surfing activities and all other sports activities in the Municipality and further providing that said surfing activities shall be managed by its Municipal Sports and Recreation Center under the Office of the Municipal Mayor. 5 G.R. No. 1920289, January 17, 2018.

Now, into the issue at hand, this Department opines that a mayor's permit is a necessary requirement before the 1 st Governor's Cup National Surfing Competition, organized by the Provincial Government, may be conducted within the jurisdiction of the Municipality of General Luna. The province interposes an argument that Section 465 (b)(l )(xix) of RA 7160, which provides that it may conduct palarong panlalawigan, is an exception for the requirement of mayor's permit. However, had the Congress intended such, it should have been expressly stated in the law. Since there was no express provision reflecting such intent, then Section 465 (b)(l )(xix) must be harmonized with the other provision of the Code on the power of the concerned LGU to regulate the activities conducted within its jurisdiction, through the issuance of mayor's permit. Nevertheless, while we are amenable that your Office has the authority to regulate the subject surfing activities conducted within the jurisdiction of your municipality, through the issuance of mayor's permit, you are hereby reminded to always exercise such authority with faimess and reasonableness. If there is an application for a mayor's permit and the applicant has already complied with all the requirements under the ordinance, then it is only proper that the mayor's permit shall be issued. You must not act with grave abuse of authority in thwarting legitimate activities of the applicant. In fact, in Lacap vs. Sandiganbayan mentioned earlier, the Supreme Court also emphasized that if the deliberate refusal to act or intentional inaction on an application for mayor's permit is motivated by personal conflicts and political considerations, the same constitutes a violation of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act. Notwithstanding the above, and considering that the activities pursued by you and Governor Barbers intend to promote surfing in Siargao and encourage tourists to visit this destination, this Level recommends that the two LGUs may coordinate in the conduct of said activities. In that manner, the manpower and resources of the two LGUs may be maximized in the conduct of the activity and ensure success thereof. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. ery ly yours, AN OR R.
